what: Route 1 run 1 (step-response probe, +120) completed its FULL 13000 ms window for the first time -- no truncation, good telemetry -- but FAILS the predeclared criteria 2a/2b: neither the step nor the settle phase reached a stable rate. Also surfaced a code bug: the service's own 'reason' field always reported 'travel_guard_tripped' regardless of whether the guard actually tripped.
verdict: FAIL. Criteria 2 (2a) and 3 (2b) fail. Per the predeclaration, 'any failure is a FAIL' -- tau_actuator_s=2.049s must NOT be quoted as a settled result.

run_1.label: baseline 3000 / step 5000 / settle 5000, +120, max_travel_m=4.0
run_1.actual_outcome: window_complete -- see bug_found below. Zero of 127 samples carry travel_guard_tripped:true, phase_transitions land exactly on schedule (0 / 3000.7 / 8000.7 ms), last sample at 13000.739 ms of a 13000 ms window, cumulative_travel_m 2.7111 of the 4.00 m budget.

analysis_raw.interpretation: tau_actuator_s = |rotation after commanding angular 0| / steady rate during the step. Compare it against the ~1 s decision period: well below means the dead time is dominated by the OBSERVER and damping cannot fix it; comparable or above means real actuator carryover.
analysis_raw.caveats: n is small by construction at ~1 Hz. Do NOT fit a turn-rate law to this, and do NOT reuse omega as a calibration constant -- the 2026-08-26 guarded-turn measurement showed a 2.6x spread on identical stationary parameters.

run_1.analysis_caveat: tau_actuator_s=2.049s and omega_step_deg_per_s=-5.5141 came out of the analysis field but do not meet criteria 2a/2b (below) and must not be quoted as a clean measurement.

1_report_stream_ready.evidence: started/continuous_started true, ready true, no readiness_reason, position_sequence advanced 99->112 across 127 samples.

2_step_reaches_steady_rotation_2a.requirement: >=3 informative intervals AND last two step rates agree within 1.5 deg/s
2_step_reaches_steady_rotation_2a.note: Rate computed as consecutive course_degrees delta / delta(midpoint_elapsed_ms). Rate was still increasing in magnitude at the end of the step phase, not settled.

3_settle_goes_flat_2b.requirement: >=3 informative intervals AND last two settle rates agree within 1.5 deg/s
3_settle_goes_flat_2b.note: Non-monotonic: rate crossed from positive (1.929) to near-zero (-0.136), the same 'chord noise on ~0.26 m chords' signature documented for the 2026-08-29 runs. Not a clean plateau.

4_containment_and_stop.evidence: 0 of 127 samples outside the 9.0 m corridor (bounds x:[1.4465,10.4465] y:[-9.6394,-0.6394]); observed x:[5.9465,7.0299] y:[-7.5996,-5.1394]. stop_result.ok=true, ack.movement_ok=true.

5_travel_guard_does_not_trip.evidence: 0 of 127 samples carry travel_guard_tripped:true; full 13000 ms window elapsed; cumulative_travel_m 2.7111 of 4.00 m budget never approached the cap.
5_travel_guard_does_not_trip.caveat: The service's own 'reason' field said 'travel_guard_tripped' at run time. That reading was WRONG -- see bug_found below. Scored here from the per-sample evidence, not the summary field.

6_gate_disarmed_after_verified.evidence: enabled:false, real_motion_allowed:false, no active session, verified from both the live API and RAW core.config_entries (enable_experimental_motion:false) after a ~15s propagation delay.

bug_found.what: `_step_response_probe_impl`'s `reason` field read `travel_abort.is_set()`, which is ALWAYS true by the time it is checked: the function's own `finally` block sets that same asyncio.Event unconditionally as part of mandatory-stop teardown (to also unblock the phase/sampler tasks), whether `_continuous_refresh_window` returned because the guard genuinely fired mid-window or because the window simply completed on schedule.
bug_found.how_found: This run's phase_transitions landed exactly on the 0/3000/8000 ms schedule and the last sample was at 13000.739 ms of a 13000 ms window -- inconsistent with an early guard trip. Checked every sample for `travel_guard_tripped:true` and found zero, confirming the top-level 'reason' field was wrong.
bug_found.fix: commit-pending: `_step_response_completion_reason()` now reads `motion_refresh['aborted_early']` instead, which `_continuous_refresh_window` sets only when its own loop observed the abort event WHILE STILL RUNNING -- the one signal that actually distinguishes a real trip from normal completion. Two unit tests pin both branches.
bug_found.scope_of_prior_evidence: Two prior evidence files (docs/evidence-dead-time-measured-20260829.json, docs/evidence-option-b-blocked-by-travel-budget-20260830.json) also recorded 'reason: travel_guard_tripped' on every real run. This bug means that field cannot be trusted retroactively on its own. It does NOT invalidate those files' conclusions where they were drawn from other evidence (informative-interval counts, course_series values, explicit 'still rotating at the last sample' observations) -- those are independent of the reason field. Not re-audited here; flagged for awareness, not re-litigated.

safety.corridor: 9.0 m square, re-scanned and re-verified at the live position (5.9465, -5.1394) immediately before dispatch, half-width 4.5 m against a required 4.50 m disk (max_travel_m 4.00 + stop_overshoot 0.50)
safety.battery_pct_at_dispatch: 48 (operator explicitly authorized proceeding despite this being below the doc's docked-and-charged precondition)
safety.gate_state: found ARMED at session start (enabled:true, real_motion_allowed:true, blockers:[]) before this run's own arming -- consistent with the operator having just repositioned the mower via the card, which needs the gate armed for Nudge; not treated as an unexplained armed-at-rest occurrence
safety.operator_confirmation: explicit go/no-go confirmation taken immediately before dispatch (on-site, supervising, area clear, blades off)

what_this_does_NOT_establish: tau_actuator_s=2.049s is NOT a settled value -- both 2a and 2b failed, meaning neither phase reached a stable rate this run captured.
n=1. This is one run at one sign (+120). Run 2 (+180) is not authorized by a FAIL and was not dispatched.

Whether a longer step/settle phase would pass 2a/2b is unknown -- step_ms is deliberately capped at 5000 per the predeclaration's own reasoning (see phase2-route1-predeclared-20260830.md section 4), so the next lever is not obvious.
what_a_pass_would_have_authorized: Writing the feed-forward design document (predeclaration section 9). This is a FAIL, so it authorizes nothing beyond recording the result.
